editorial.headline: Financial Market Advice: Open Nationally, Closed to PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: This advisory activity is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks registration at a Bali address.
editorial.body:
For a Bali address, the starting point is blunt: a foreign investor cannot register this activity there today. That conclusion sits beside, not against, the national setting. Nationally, Other Financial Market Advisory Activities is open to foreign investment, with foreign ownership permitted up to 100%. Bali’s status is closed under the PMA moratorium, so the national opening does not translate into a PMA registration route on the island.

The activity itself is a broad home for financial-support work not classified elsewhere. It includes financial consulting; mortgage advisory and brokerage; mortgage consulting; and other investment advisory services. The record specifically names robo-advisor services as an example. Taken together, the scope describes advice and advisory intermediation across financial and mortgage matters, including technology-enabled investment guidance, rather than a single narrow professional service. Its breadth matters: several advisory forms sit within one declared activity without being confined to one delivery model.

Registration is open across every stated business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That broad scale availability is national context; it does not dissolve Bali’s local PMA position. The record identifies the Besar scale as Menengah Rendah. Under Bali’s island-wide, permanent PMA moratorium, all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities are blocked where registration uses a Bali address. The decisive Bali fact is therefore not whether the advisory work is delivered conventionally or through a robo-advisor, but that its stated risk treatment brings it within the moratorium.

The record must be read in two layers. The national layer says the activity is TERBUKA and allows a foreign stake of up to 100%. The Bali layer says PMA registration is blocked for a Bali address because of the moratorium. Both statements are true at once; neither overrides the other. For a proposal centred on Bali, the address is the point at which the national permission stops being actionable. The code remains the description for the listed advisory activities, but it is not a current PMA-registration path in Bali.
editorial.pullQuote: A national 100% foreign-ownership ceiling does not create a PMA registration path in Bali under the island-wide moratorium.
